quote: Rational agents make decisions that maximize the probabilistic expectation of a coherent utility function
content: The Allais and Ellsberg violations are the reason the axioms are normative rather than descriptive, not a refutation of them. Each violation is exploitable: an agent with those preferences can be offered a sequence of trades it accepts and which leaves it strictly worse off, and the money-pump literature treats this as the argument for the axioms rather than a curiosity (Gustafsson 2022, Money-Pump Arguments, book, no DOI). The alternatives named here do not escape the framework, they refine it: dropping completeness yields representation by a set of utility functions, so the agent still maximizes, just not uniquely (Dubra, Maccheroni & Ok 2004), and Buchak’s risk-weighted theory is itself an expectation of a utility function under a transformed probability. A contested boundary is not a contested center.

quote: No one can actually calculate and obey the math, any more than you can predict the stock market by calculating the movements of quarks.
content: This confuses a norm with an algorithm. No chess player can compute the game-theoretic value of a position either, and that has never made the word "blunder" empty; the optimal play defines the direction in which approximations are better or worse. Gigerenzer’s own case for simple heuristics is made in terms of predictive accuracy under a bias–variance decomposition, which is to say it is scored against exactly the correspondence standard the essay proposes and the annotation says is unusable. The essay does ask the question of what a bounded agent should do, at length, in the four books that follow; the answer given there is that you approximate the ideal with the resources you have, which is what "no one can obey the math" was said to introduce.

quote: the judgment that P(Bill plays jazz) is less than P(Bill plays jazz, Bill is an accountant) is labeled incorrect
content: The frequency-format result narrows the effect without dissolving it. Conjunction violations survive when subjects bet real money on the outcome, when the two options are presented side by side so that the set relation is transparent, and in between-subjects designs that remove the conversational implicature entirely (Sides, Osherson, Bonini & Viale 2002). Tentori and Crupi’s confirmation-based account, offered here as a rival, is an account of why the fallacy occurs, not a demonstration that the judgment is correct. Whatever the mechanism, P(A&B) > P(A) remains a violation of the probability axioms, and the essay’s claim was only that it is one.
